name: Shadow IT — Unsanctioned SaaS Wired Into Corp SSO
description: An eager team lead spins up a free Notion workspace, enables 'sign in with Microsoft', and starts inviting external contractors. Three weeks later 142 corp users are signed in, internal customer notes are pasted in, and security has no idea.
reasoning: The corp identity edge starts seeing a steady trickle of OAuth sign-ins to a previously-unseen application ID. CASB flags it; the simulation focuses on detection, not exploitation.

narrative.text: Day-1 baseline. Notion sees 4 monthly sign-ins from a couple of usual rebels.
Volume creeps up: team lead invites 14 contractors, OAuth grants spike.
By day 7, 73 users are signed in; notes from internal Confluence are being pasted in.
By day 14, 142 users; CASB risk score for 'notion.so' rises into the 'review' band.
Security risk-review meeting — they take ownership: either sanction it or block it.
Decision: sanction it under enterprise plan with SCIM + DLP. Shadow path closed within 7 days.
All steady; long-term policy: monthly automated CASB review of new SaaS apps.
